english.html: ly as all are vain and ridiculous, proceeding from the wiles of Satan, and rejected not only by the express commandment of God, repeated in a hundred places, under threat of death <sup class="mk" data-key="r">r</sup>, but also by the human laws (of which, nevertheless, the greater part of the authors were heathens), under the like penalty <sup class="mk" data-key="ſ">ſ</sup>. This most great, most good and most mighty God has given us the word of His Gospel, to which in our adversities we may withdraw, take counsel and be comforted; and not inquire into things that do not belong to us — as Abraham answered, holding Lazarus in his bosom, to the wicked Rich Man who was in the torments of hell and begged him to send Lazarus to his brothers: They have Moses (said Abraham) and the Prophets; if your brothers will not believe them, neither will they believe though one of the dead should rise again <sup class="mk" data-key="t">t</sup>. Let us not permit, then, that Satan — who raises his horns day and night, and spreads these dangerous fowling-nets to entangle us by this means in his meshes, from which Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, has so dearly redeemed us by the incomprehensible pains and torments of His passion — should impose upon us in this matter and seduce us; but in such or like temptation let us always withdraw to our Redeemer, and most humbly beseech Him that He will set our hearts aright and lead us in His ways, so that by the light of His word we may drive from us all illusions, juggleries and impostures (with which the devil, who seeks always to catch us, incessantly lays new ambushes against the children of God and His Church).
